summary: Radar for 2026-10-13, GLP-1 focus only. The plague lane from earlier snapshots has been dropped. The biggest story today is retatrutide. Google Trends shows US search interest for "retatrutide" (about 200+ searches). CBS News also reported this morning that the FDA received two death reports naming bootleg "Reta" as a suspect product. CBS says the details aren't verified and it's unclear whether the drug was to blame. That fits our proven myth-bust format about online products (55 views), and we can pair it with a separate decoder of the real TRIUMPH-2 trial data (Lilly-reported: 20.8% weight loss on the top dose vs 4.0% on placebo at 80 weeks, adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes). Fresh peer-reviewed or congress hooks: semaglutide cut heavy-drinking days in alcohol use disorder with obesity (Lancet RCT), semaglutide and epigenetic aging clocks (MIT Tech Review on Oct 6, plus NewsNation and KRDO now), and nail detachment in GLP-1 users (EADV abstract, not peer reviewed, rising across Yahoo, ScienceDaily and Medical Independent). Evergreen pieces with a fresh hook: protecting muscle (our best cross-platform topic, refreshed by IBIO-610 and frailty data), Wegovy pill vs Foundayo (orforglipron) pill, sleep apnea and nausea habits. I verified that the "FDA approves Lilly's weight-loss pill" headline in today's feed refers to Foundayo's April 1, 2026 approval, so it's not new news. The weight-regain pilot RCT and EloraTZP were left out or ranked low because we covered them recently (S3 10-13 and the long-form). Status lines to date: retatrutide, EloraTZP and CagriSema are investigational as of Oct 2026. Korean NAION and pancreatitis reports were skipped because safety-scare topics underperform for us and the case data is thin.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2: 20.8% weight loss on top dose vs 4.0% placebo at 80 weeks in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes (Lilly-reported)
candidates.angle: A named-drug decoder: 'What did retatrutide actually do in TRIUMPH-2?' We'll explain the triple agonist (GLP-1, GIP and glucagon) simply, give the dose arms (12.7% / 19.1% / 20.8%), up to 1.6% A1C drop vs 0.2%, and 14% discontinuation on the top dose. TRIUMPH-2 is placebo-controlled, not head-to-head with tirzepatide, and the results come from Lilly's release. Investigational as of Oct 2026. This pairs with the Reta myth-bust: the real trial vs the bootleg vial.
candidates.why_now: Search interest is trending. The Clinical Trial Vanguard published a TRIUMPH-2 piece today, and the Women's Health and SciTechDaily pieces are recent. The CBS bootleg story will send people searching for what the real drug does. Named-drug decoders are our proven long-form format.

candidates.topic: Semaglutide cut heavy-drinking days in adults with alcohol use disorder and obesity (Lancet RCT, 108 people, 26 weeks)
candidates.angle: 'Can semaglutide (Wegovy) change your drinking?' We'll explain the brain reward pathway, then the number: heavy-drinking days fell 41.1 points vs 26.4 on placebo (difference 13.7 points). Everyone also got CBT. The population is AUD plus obesity, and semaglutide isn't approved for alcohol use. Mention common GI side effects. If drinking is a concern, talk to a clinician; for UK viewers, add helplines with their real hours.
candidates.why_now: Lancet publication and Medical Economics ran it on Oct 11. 'Ozempic and alcohol' is a heavily searched question, and this is a high-quality RCT. It's a 'what does it do to my body/brain' question, which is our winning type.
